title: -er/-ir dot past: -í, -ió; más que yo; nada, nadie; durar, durante, sin parar

cards.title: -er / -ir dot past: comí, comió
cards.body: -í for I, -ió for he/she/it/formal you, both stressed.

examples.en: I don't know why she hasn't left yet.
examples.es: No sé por qué no salió todavía.

cards.title: que = than; más que yo
cards.body: Spanish is literal: 'more than he (ate)', 'more than I'. English 'me!' for 'I do!' is negative transfer to watch for.

examples.en: I saw him, but he didn't see me.
examples.es: (Yo) lo vi, pero (él) no me vio.

cards.title: nada, nadie — double negatives
cards.body: Spanish uses double negatives: 'I didn't see nothing'.

cards.title: durar; durante = during / for
cards.body: Endure, duration, even 'Duracell': brand names use Latin to appeal to you. Durante works like the -ante adjectives and can mean 'for' a time. Media hora = half an hour.

examples.en: He ate for half an hour.

cards.title: sin parar = without stopping
cards.body: Sin = without; after it, use the 'to' form. Parar (to stop) links to par (a pair): com-parar, pre-parar, re-pair, se-parar ('pair apart').

examples.en: He talked for half an hour without stopping.
examples.es: Habló durante media hora sin parar.
